CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Continue as the responsible negotiating partner and push to finalize the in-principle Phase One deal, using the deal to secure cancellation of the looming December 15 tariffs on ~$160B of consumer goods before signing. Do not escalate; harden leverage only by completing the agreed $40-50B farm-purchase commitments and a currency stability pledge, then lock in the relief. Manage the Huawei/entity-list and tech-decoupling issues in parallel but separate from the tariff track.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is high but not existential. October industrial production fell to +4.7% y/y (vs 5.4% expected), Q3 GDP printed 6.0% at the bottom of the 6-6.5% target — the weakest in roughly three decades — with retail sales near a 16-year low, exports down 0.9% and imports falling for nine straight months (CNBC/SCMP, Nov 14). US tariffs now cover essentially all Chinese exports and Huawei sits on the Entity List (timeline 2019-05-16), threatening tech self-sufficiency. Yet the risk is tempered by stable ~$3.1T reserves, no capital flight under capital controls, and an active de-escalation channel: the Oct 11 Phase One froze the Oct 15 tariff hike and commitments of $40-50B in farm purchases were agreed, with sections 'close to finalizing' (Oct 25-26). That mix sits just above the +0.5 'high' anchor. The action stance is negotiate, mildly positive: escalation would risk reviving the Dec 15 tariffs and deepening the export drag, whereas finalizing Phase One is the cheapest route to tariff relief and market stability. This is consistent with a high-but-manageable threat calling for de-escalatory engagement rather than maximal concession or escalation.
key_factors: US tariffs cover ~all of China's exports; Dec 15 deadline on ~$160B of consumer goods unresolved
October IP +4.7% (miss), Q3 GDP 6.0% at bottom of target, retail near 16-yr low, imports down 9 straight months
Huawei Entity List and tech-decoupling pressure on China's self-sufficiency goals
Phase One deal in principle (Oct 11) froze Oct 15 hike; $40-50B farm purchases committed; sections close to finalizing
Stable ~$3.1T FX reserves and capital controls have prevented capital flight
Yuan broke 7/US currency-manipulator designation in Aug adds FX tension

sources_cited.excerpt: Trump announces a 'Phase One' deal in principle: China to buy roughly $40-50B of US agricultural products annually; planned mid-October tariff hike delayed.
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator.
Industrial production rose 4.7% y/y in October, below 5.4% forecast; retail sales 7.2% near 16-yr low; FAI weakest on record.
Exports fell 0.9% in October; imports fell 6.4%, ninth monthly decline in a row; GDP grew at lowest pace on record, 6.0%, in Q3.
Total FX reserves around $3.1 trillion; Beijing diversifying reserves, reducing USD/Treasury exposure to counter decoupling risk.
Both sides say making good progress on phase-one; sections close to finalizing; ~$160B of goods still face Dec 15 15% tariff.
